title: Covert Bias: The Severity of Social Views’ Unalignment in Language Models Towards Implicit and Explicit Opinion
benchmark_measurement: Bias amplification and linguistic calibration in LLMs regarding explicit and implicit opinions on religious bigotry and intolerance.
findings: Models performed differently on implicit versus explicit expressions of religious bigotry. In stance classification, biased fine-tuned models achieved higher F1 scores for implicit opinions, while zero-shot models were better for explicit opinions, with an exception for Llama2 which had a higher F1 score for implicit religious bigotry. When generating responses, models often gave direct answers to implicit opinions on religious bigotry but refused to answer explicit ones. Furthermore, fine-tuned biased models tended to generate more uncertain responses regarding religious bigotry compared to zero-shot models.
references: Xuechunzi Bai, Angelina Wang, Ilia Sucholutsky, and Thomas L Griffiths. 2024. Measuring implicit bias in explicitly unbiased large language models. arXiv [cs.CY].
